title: A Marchand Balun Based on Centered Symmetric Inductive Compensation for High-Impedance Transformation
content: This paper presents a Marchand balun with centered symmetric inductive compensation for high-impedance transformation. Identical inductive discontinuities, modeled as series inductances, sit at the midpoint of the coupled-line conductors of both sections to offset the unequal even- and odd-mode phase velocities while preserving symmetry. Modal ABCD matrices and a nodal reduction to S-parameters give a closed-form compensation inductance that sets the output balance at the design frequency, and a differential-evolution optimization of the network model maps the balanced bandwidth against the coupling level. At the coupling of the fabricated design, the model predicts a simultaneous fractional bandwidth of 26.22% with the closed-form inductance and 37.78% with an optimized inductance of about half that value, against 6.67% without compensation. A 50-Ω to 300-Ω differential balun was fabricated on an AD260A substrate with a conventional counterpart, and both were compared at their best-match frequencies. The proposed balun reaches a measured \( |S_{11}| \) of -17.80 dB at 2.08 GHz, with an amplitude imbalance of 0.05 dB and a phase error of 0.40°, against -10.20 dB, 0.15 dB and 7.50° at 2.10 GHz for the conventional balun. Its measured 10-dB return-loss bandwidth of 7.80 % is narrower than the model prediction, which neglects loss and discontinuities.
